{"items": [
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Maryland's expectation is clear: AI use must never compromise student privacy or weaken data protections.", "force": "prohibition", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "All AI use in Maryland schools must comply with federal and state privacy and civil rights laws, including FERPA, COPPA, PPRA, and applicable Maryland regulations.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "All AI use in Maryland schools", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Schools must be transparent with families about how AI tools handle student data.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Schools", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Maryland expects districts to minimize data collection by limiting student data shared with AI systems, avoiding entry of personally identifiable information into generative tools unless explicitly approved, restricting unnecessary data access, and providing alternatives when AI use is inappropriate.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "districts", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": "unless explicitly approved"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Collection of biometric, behavioral, or location data is prohibited unless legally required and educationally justified.", "force": "prohibition", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": "unless legally required and educationally justified"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Districts must implement robust system protections, including secure authentication, encryption, vendor security requirements, staff training, and tested incident response plans.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Districts", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "AI systems must operate with documented human oversight.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "AI systems", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": "documented human oversight"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Any AI-supported decision affecting students requires human review, clear procedures for addressing errors or harm, and regular audits for bias, accuracy, and unintended data collection.", "force": "obligation", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": "human review"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Districts must clearly communicate what AI tools are used, what data are collected, how long data are retained, and when opt-out options apply, using accessible and culturally responsive formats.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Districts", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "AI vendors must meet strict privacy, security, and transparency standards.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "AI vendors", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Districts must ensure contractual limits on data use, retention, and deletion; prohibit advertising, profiling, or unrelated model training; require disclosure of data practices; and ensure compliance with breach notification laws.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Districts", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": "contractual limits on data use, retention, and deletion"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Vendors that cannot demonstrate secure, education-focused data practices must not be used.", "force": "prohibition", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "reference", "text": "FERPA", "cited_instrument": "FERPA"},
{"type": "reference", "text": "COPPA", "cited_instrument": "COPPA"},
{"type": "reference", "text": "PPRA", "cited_instrument": "PPRA"},
{"type": "reference", "text": "U.S. Department of Education, 2024", "cited_instrument": "U.S. Department of Education (2024)"}
]}

{"items":[{"type":"obligation","text":"Artificial intelligence should enhance, not replace, the educators, counselors, and school leaders who remain Maryland's primary decision makers.","force":"recommendation","binds":null,"responsible_party_stated":false,"mechanism_stated":null},{"type":"obligation","text":"Maryland is committed to ensuring equitable access to AI-supported learning opportunities and to protecting student data through clear communication, human oversight, and compliance with all state and federal privacy, cybersecurity, and ethical standards.","force":"obligation","binds":"Maryland","responsible_party_stated":true,"mechanism_stated":null},{"type":"obligation","text":"This guidance will be reviewed and updated regularly to reflect research, implementation experience, and feedback, ensuring AI strengthens educational opportunities, protects human dignity, and prepares all students for success in a complex technology-driven future.","force":"obligation","binds":null,"responsible_party_stated":false,"mechanism_stated":"regularly"},{"type":"definition","term":"Artificial intelligence (AI)","text":"Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to computational systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence, including pattern recognition, content generation, prediction, and adaptive output."},{"type":"definition","term":"Machine learning","text":"Machine learning is a subset of AI in which systems improve performance by identifying patterns in data."},{"type":"definition","term":"Generative AI","text":"Generative AI produces new content such as text, images, audio, video, or code in response to user input."},{"type":"definition","term":"Large language models (LLM)","text":"Large language models (LLM) are a type of generative AI that produce text based on statistical patterns in training data and do not possess understanding or intent."},{"type":"definition","term":"AI literacy","text":"AI literacy refers to the knowledge and skills needed to understand, evaluate, and use AI responsibly, including awareness of limitations, bias, and appropriate use."},{"type":"definition","term":"Assistive AI tools","text":"Assistive AI tools support accessibility and instructional access, instructional AI tools support teaching and learning, and operational AI tools support school and district functions."},{"type":"definition","term":"Instructional AI tools","text":"Assistive AI tools support accessibility and instructional access, instructional AI tools support teaching and learning, and operational AI tools support school and district functions."},{"type":"definition","term":"Operational AI tools","text":"Assistive AI tools support accessibility and instructional access, instructional AI tools support teaching and learning, and operational AI tools support school and district functions."}]}

"force": "obligation", "binds": "Students", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null}, {"type": "obligation", "text": "All AI-assisted operational decisions that affect student clearly with families about operational AI use, evaluate systems for bias before adoption, monitor performance and impacts over time, limit use to approved educational purposes, and maintain procedures for addressing inaccurate or harmful outputs.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Districts", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": "maintain procedures for addressing inaccurate or harmful outputs"}, {"type": "obligation", "text": "Maryland will support districts through model policies, guidance, professional learning, vetted resources, and reporting mechanisms to ensure operational AI strengthens equitable, transparent, and student-centered school system functioning.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Maryland", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": "model policies, guidance, professional learning, vetted resources, and reporting mechanisms"}, {"type": "definition", "term": "Operational AI", "text": "Operational AI includes tools that rely on predictive modeling, classification, or automation to support functions such as attendance and early-warning systems, enrollment forecasting, scheduling, transportation, automated communication, and security monitoring."}]}

{"items": [
{"type": "obligation", "text": "AI should be used to support engagement with complex ideas, provide appropriate scaffolding and feedback, and personalize learning in ways that respect student identity and experience.", "force": "recommendation", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "It must not be used to bypass learning goals or substitute for essential skill development.", "force": "prohibition", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "student use must always occur within structures that promote original thinking and academic honesty.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "student use", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Learning tasks should be intentionally designed so that student reasoning, analysis, reflection, and decision making are essential and visible.", "force": "recommendation", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Students should learn to use AI transparently and responsibly.", "force": "recommendation", "binds": "Students", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "When AI use is permitted, students must acknowledge its role and be able to explain how outputs were evaluated, modified, or integrated into their own work.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "students", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Misrepresenting AI- generated content as original work constitutes a violation of academic integrity.", "force": "prohibition", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "These tools must be used in compliance with federal and state civil rights laws and cannot replace required accommodations, specialized instruction, or professional judgment.", "force": "obligation", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Decisions about AI use for students with disabilities or multilingual learners should be made collaboratively with appropriate educators and families.", "force": "recommendation", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": "collaboratively with appropriate educators and families"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Educators guide all student use of AI.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Educators", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "They establish expectations, model critical evaluation, monitor impacts on equity and learning, and ensure that AI does not overshadow disciplinary knowledge or relationships.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Educators", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Student use of AI must also support safe and ethical learning environments.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Student use of AI", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Schools should set clear expectations related to data privacy, bias awareness, digital citizenship, and reporting concerns.", "force": "recommendation", "binds": "Schools", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "definition", "term": "AI literacy", "text": "AI literacy includes understanding how AI systems function, evaluating their limitations and bias, using AI ethically, and applying these tools in academic and real-world contexts."}
]}

{"items": [
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Artificial intelligence tools used in Maryland schools must meet high standards for safety, transparency, privacy, equity, and educational value.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Artificial intelligence tools used in Maryland schools", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Because AI products vary widely in data practices, accuracy, and risk, procurement processes must ensure that tools support learning and operations without compromising student rights or causing harm (Kumar et al., 2022).", "force": "obligation", "binds": "procurement processes", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Maryland requires rigorous vendor vetting, strong contractual protections, documented risk assessments, and ongoing monitoring.", "force": "obligation", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Procurement decisions must align with state goals, legal requirements, equity priorities, and responsible data stewardship, consistent with federal guidance on ethical AI adoption in education (U.S. Department of Education, 2023).", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Procurement decisions", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "reference", "text": "U.S. Department of Education, 2023", "cited_instrument": "U.S. Department of Education (2023) federal guidance on ethical AI adoption in education"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Districts must prioritize tools with clear educational or operational value, transparent data practices, compliance with FERPA, COPPA, state privacy laws, and civil rights protections, and demonstrated attention to bias, fairness, and accessibility.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Districts", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "reference", "text": "FERPA", "cited_instrument": "FERPA"},
{"type": "reference", "text": "COPPA", "cited_instrument": "COPPA"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "To support consistent practice, Maryland will provide vendor vetting rubrics, model contract language, a centralized list of vetted tools, professional learning, technical assistance, and reporting mechanisms to ensure statewide AI procurement protects students and upholds equity, transparency, and legal compliance.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Maryland", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Vendors must provide clear documentation on AI techniques, data collection and retention, use of data for model training, known limitations, accessibility and nondiscrimination measures, and evaluation populations.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Vendors", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Tools that lack sufficient transparency must not be adopted.", "force": "prohibition", "binds": "Tools that lack sufficient transparency", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Contracts must include data minimization, limits on data use and sharing, security and breach response requirements, bias mitigation, audit rights, and clear termination and data deletion provisions.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Contracts", "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": null},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "After adoption, districts must monitor AI tools for performance, bias, and unintended impacts; review vendor updates; respond to harmful outputs; and report significant concerns to MSDE.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "districts", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": "report significant concerns to MSDE"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Before approval, districts must conduct documented risk assessments addressing data sensitivity, potential bias or inaccuracy, appropriateness for minors, transparency, and potential impacts on student placement, grading, discipline, or access to opportunity.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "districts", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": "Before approval"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "Higher-risk tools require additional review and may be restricted or prohibited.", "force": "obligation", "binds": null, "responsible_party_stated": false, "mechanism_stated": "additional review"},
{"type": "obligation", "text": "As technologies evolve, Maryland will adapt policies, support local implementation, and engage educators, students, and families.", "force": "obligation", "binds": "Maryland", "responsible_party_stated": true, "mechanism_stated": null}
]}
